title: What Good Governance Looks Like
summary: What governance is for in a regulated firm or fund, what good, bad and failed governance look like in practice, and why governing a fund or licensee differs from governing an ordinary company.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What governance is for in a regulated firm or fund, what good, bad and failed governance look like in practice, and why governing a fund or licensee differs from governing an ordinary company.
Learning Objectives: Define governance in terms of the interests the board must serve
Distinguish good, poor and failed governance using real enforcement outcomes
Map the parties around the board: owners, regulators, managers and delegates
Syllabus: Purpose of governance: acting efficiently and exclusively in investors' and customers' interests
Good governance: clear responsibilities, documented policies and structures that foster challenge
When governance fails: lessons from regulatory fines and misconduct cases
The distinctive features of fund and regulated-firm governance
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated firms, fund boards and management companies
Senior managers preparing for a first board appointment or moving from an executive to a non-executive role
Company secretaries, heads of governance and compliance staff who support the board and its committees
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
